symptoms: Global route overflow > 5% concentrated in specific macro channels or block boundaries.
Detailed route fails with massive spacing/short violations in lower metal layers (M1-M3) localized to specific bounding boxes.
Placement utilization > 85% overall but local pin density > 95% in specific regions.

candidate_causes.cause: Macro placement creates narrow channels with high pin density.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Plot GRT congestion map overlaid with macro bounding boxes; if red hotspots align with channel edges between large SRAMs, it is macro-channel congestion.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add routing blockages to force detours, shift macros to widen channels, or use partial placement blockages.

candidate_causes.cause: High pin-density standard cells clustered together.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Extract cell density map for high-pin-count cells; if hotspot correlates with logic cones of complex functions like bus muxes, it is cell-level congestion.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Spread logic via placement padding, or swap to lower-pin-count equivalent cells if timing allows.

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient upper-layer routing resources allocated to block.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check layer availability; if M4-M6 are blocked by top-level power straps or routing blockages, local congestion is forced into lower layers.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Negotiate top-level routing layer assignment or add local routing blockages to push wires to higher layers.

candidate_causes.cause: Excessive feedthrough routing through block.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check terminal assignments; if many pins are on opposite sides of the block and internal logic is sparse in the middle, it is feedthrough.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-pin the block or add dedicated routing channels.

ordering_rationale: Check macro and boundary constraints first because they are the cheapest to identify and hardest to fix late in the flow.
classic_trap: Blaming the global router for bad heuristics when the placement is physically unroutable due to macro channel starvation.

symptoms: WNS is highly negative with TNS dominated by a few thousand paths sharing a common startpoint or clock.
WNS is moderate but TNS is massive, with failing paths spread uniformly across the design indicating a logic-depth problem.
WNS is localized exclusively to paths crossing hierarchy boundaries or clock domain crossings.

candidate_causes.cause: Unrealistic clock tree insertion delay or skew target at block boundary.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check the SDC boundary budget; if the arrival time at the block pin minus the required time equals the WNS exactly, the budget is too tight.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Renegotiate block boundary budget or adjust top-level clock latency.

candidate_causes.cause: Logic depth too high for the target clock period.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Path histogram shows a wall of paths failing by roughly the same amount; no single bottleneck gate stands out.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Pipeline the logic, restructure RTL, or accept a slower clock.

candidate_causes.cause: Placement congestion causing massive detours and high wire delays.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check wire delay percentage in the timing report; if wire delay > 60% of total path delay and correlates with GRT congestion hotspots, it is congestion-induced.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Fix placement congestion or use useful skew.

candidate_causes.cause: Overly pessimistic OCV/AOCV derating on logically common paths.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare WNS across corners; if it only fails on a specific slow corner with high OCV penalties, check if the path is logically common.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Apply path-specific or stage-specific SOCV/AOCV derating.

ordering_rationale: Check boundary budgets and path histograms first to separate constraint errors from fundamental logic-depth issues before attempting local optimizations.
classic_trap: Upsizing cells on a logic-depth problem, which only adds capacitance and worsens the WNS on the preceding stages.

symptoms: Massive hold violations appearing immediately after CTS, mostly on short paths or scan chains.
Localized hold violations clustered around specific clock tree buffers or macro pins.
Hold violations that appear only after detailed routing due to wire delay changes.

candidate_causes.cause: Clock tree skew is too large locally.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Plot clock insertion delays for launch and capture flops; if the delta is highly negative and localized to one clock branch, it is local CTS skew.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add clock tree constraints to balance that specific branch, or use useful skew.

candidate_causes.cause: Scan chain ordering creates extremely short paths between adjacent scan flops.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check if failing paths are exclusively scan_in to scan_out with zero logic levels; if yes, it is a scan chain hold issue.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert lockup latches or rely on scan compression tool to reorder and insert buffers.

candidate_causes.cause: Missing or insufficient min_delay constraints.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Run timing with min delay report; if paths have no constraints and default to zero, the SDC is incomplete.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add proper set_min_delay or set_false_path for hold.

candidate_causes.cause: Crosstalk delay causing effective hold violations.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Run SI-aware timing vs non-SI; if hold WNS drops significantly only with SI enabled, it is crosstalk-induced (more common at 28nm and below).
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Space out aggressor and victim nets, or insert shielding.

ordering_rationale: Check clock skew and scan chains first because they account for the vast majority of post-CTS hold violations and are cheap to diagnose.
classic_trap: Inserting hold buffers globally without checking if the violation is actually caused by local clock skew, which just adds area and power.

symptoms: Dynamic IR drop hotspots > 10% of VDD localized to specific regions during switching activity.
Static IR drop showing gradual voltage sag from power pads or bumps to the center of the die.
Timing degradation that only appears when IR-drop aware timing analysis is enabled.

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient power strap density or width in the hotspot region.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay IR drop map with power grid map; if the hotspot aligns with a gap between wide upper-layer power straps, it is grid starvation.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add local power straps, widen existing ones, or add decap cells.

candidate_causes.cause: High localized switching activity.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check toggle rates; if a specific module toggles at > 50% while others are < 10%, it is a localized activity hotspot.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Spread the logic, add decap, or reduce toggle rate via RTL changes.

candidate_causes.cause: Missing or high-resistance bumps in the package model.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check the static IR drop gradient; if the entire die sags uniformly and the gradient starts at the die edge, it is a package or bump issue.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add more power bumps or improve package power planes.

candidate_causes.cause: Decap placement is too far from the switching instances.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Measure distance from decap cells to the IR drop hotspot; if > 50um, the decap is ineffective for high-frequency dynamic droop.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Move decap cells closer to the high-toggle-rate instances.

ordering_rationale: Check local grid density and toggle rates first because they are the most common causes of localized dynamic droop and easiest to map visually.
classic_trap: Adding decap cells randomly across the floorplan instead of targeting the specific high-frequency switching hotspots.

symptoms: Clock tree fails to meet target insertion delay or skew limits.
Max transition or max capacitance violations on clock buffers.
Clock tree routing fails with massive shorts or cannot be routed within the allocated blockages.

candidate_causes.cause: Clock tree structure has unbalanced branch lengths or fanouts.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report clock tree structure; if one branch drives thousands of flops and another drives hundreds, it is a structural imbalance.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add clock tree constraints to guide clustering, or add dummy flops to balance load.

candidate_causes.cause: Excessive clock gating cells creating huge local fanouts.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check fanout of ICGs; if a single ICG drives > 200 flops and causes local skew, it is ICG overloading (very common at 7nm/5nm due to multi-bit ICGs).
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Clone the ICG, break it into smaller banks, or use multi-bit ICGs.

candidate_causes.cause: Clock routing blockages are too aggressive or misplaced.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check clock DRCs and routing congestion; if clock buffers are pushed into tiny slivers of whitespace and fail transition, it is blockage-induced.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax clock routing blockages or create dedicated clock channels.

candidate_causes.cause: Incorrect clock tree models or inaccurate RC tech file.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare pre-CTS estimated skew vs post-CTS actual skew; if they diverge wildly, the estimation models are wrong.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Update wireload models or use physical-aware CTS.

ordering_rationale: Check structural fanouts and ICG loading first because they are the root cause of most local skew and DRC issues in modern nodes.
classic_trap: Tightening global skew targets to fix a local hotspot, which causes the CTS tool to insert massive amounts of buffering and wreck the design area.

symptoms: Detailed routing finishes but reports thousands of spacing or short violations on specific lower layers.
Max transition or max capacitance violations on signal nets post-route.
Antenna violations on long lower-layer routes.

candidate_causes.cause: Placement congestion forcing router to use lower layers where design rules are tighter.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check DRC layer distribution; if 90% of spacing violations are on M2/M3 in a specific bounding box, it is local placement congestion.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Fix placement congestion, add routing blockages on lower layers to force higher layers.

candidate_causes.cause: Non-Default Rules applied too aggressively.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check if DRCs are on nets with NDRs like double-width or spacing; if yes, the NDR is starving the router of resources.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax NDRs for non-critical nets, or use partial NDRs.

candidate_causes.cause: Missing or incorrect technology LEF spacing rules.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check if violations are systematic across the entire die on a specific layer; if yes, suspect LEF rule issues like missing parallel run length tables.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Fix the LEF file with foundry-corrected rules.

candidate_causes.cause: High fanout nets routed as daisy-chains causing max transition violations.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check max transition DRCs; if they occur on nets with fanout > 50, it is a high-fanout net buffering issue.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert buffers during placement or synthesis, or use tree-routing.

ordering_rationale: Check layer distribution and NDRs first because they quickly separate localized congestion issues from global constraint misconfigurations.
classic_trap: Running the detailed router with higher effort levels to fix spacing violations that are actually caused by fundamental placement congestion.
